seedTerms: A fear or phobia rearing its head

premise.headline: A dinosaur expert meets her final boss: a pigeon.

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Commitment Fossil
seedTermsUsed: A fear or phobia rearing its head
jokes.joke: I dated a palaeontologist, and on the third date she asked my biggest fear. I said, “Commitment.” She got excited. Apparently my emotional availability had been extinct for 65 million years, but she thought she could identify it from a tiny fragment of jaw.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Bone Dry
seedTermsUsed: A fear or phobia rearing its head
jokes.joke: I started dating a palaeontologist. Seemed great — smart, passionate, outdoorsy. Then I find out she's terrified of birds. Not like 'ooh, that crow startled me.' I mean full panic attack at a pigeon. This woman has spent thirty years lovingly excavating dinosaurs, and their direct living descendants give her a breakdown. I didn't say anything. But I thought it. Loudly.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Sibling Rivalry
jokes.joke: I’m a palaeontologist, but I'm incredibly resentful of my older brother, the ER surgeon. At family dinners, he tells these dramatic stories about pulling people back from the brink of death. Everyone cries and applauds. Then all eyes go to me, and I have to try and sound heroic explaining how I spent six months in a desert using a toothbrush to find a lizard that failed to survive an asteroid.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Sports Resentment
jokes.joke: Folks, I've been a die-hard sports fan my whole life, but lately I'm getting seriously resentful. I yell at the TV, skip parties to watch games, and invest all this emotional energy like it's my job. Then my team blows another lead in the final minutes. For what? Another ruined weekend. At this point, I should just root for the other guys—at least I'd be happy when we lose.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: The Cliffside Game
jokes.joke: I tried to impress a date by saying I’m really into extreme sports. She asked what kind, and I panicked and said, “Uh… competitive waterfall watching.” So now I’m standing on a cliff, soaked, pretending I can judge splash technique. She’s like, “Is this real?” and I’m like, “Absolutely. I’m giving that one a 9 for commitment—because it’s the only one of us not lying right now.”

scores.comment: Clear comic contradiction with a smart paleontology angle; the final beat is amusing but softer than the premise.
Strong contrast, clean escalation, and a good final image; the asteroid line carries the joke well.
Relatable and coherent, but the sports-fan misery angle is familiar and the turn is expected.
Fun absurd premise with a decent self-own at the end, though the wording is a little long and the payoff is not sharp enough for a 7.
Clean concept, nice escalation from commitment joke to fossil metaphor. The jaw fragment payoff is specific and earns its landing. A little cerebral but the turn is genuinely non-obvious.
Solid sibling rivalry premise with a well-observed contrast. The toothbrush-lizard-asteroid line is the real joke and it delivers. Setup runs slightly long but the final image saves it.
The premise is familiar sports-fan grievance and the turn — root for the other team — is the first obvious destination. Competent filler but nothing surprises or sticks.

Absurdist but grounded in a relatable panic situation. 'Competitive waterfall watching' earns its laugh and the final line gives the waterfall itself the punchline, which is a nice inversion. Slightly shaggy in the middle.
The premise is standard, and the punchline feels like a forced, slightly clunky metaphor rather than a natural stand-up observation.
Excellent stage rhythm and a genuinely smart, grounded observation about the profession. The tag perfectly caps the built-in irony.
Opens with a hacky 'Folks...' and proceeds to just list generic sports fan complaints. It lacks a true comedic turn or punchline.
Delightfully absurd imagery in the setup, but the final tag is slightly convoluted and blunts what could have been a sharper laugh.
Clever extinct pun, natural seeds, solid chuckle.
Strong dinosaur-bird irony, very funny payoff.
Good job contrast but predictable resentment angle.
Absurd premise works but feels a bit forced at end.
Clear premise and clean wording; turn is mild but works.
Good contrast between profession and fear; solid, mildly funny payoff.
Well‑structured and relatable; punchline is competent but not sharp.
Recognizable premise but predictable; ending restates the setup.
